questions.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $\frac{10-8a}{5}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Splitting the fraction into separate terms and then simplifying the fractions in individual terms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{10-8a}{5} & = \\ \frac{10}{5}-\frac{8a}{5} & = \\ 2-\frac{8a}{5} & .\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Splitting the fraction into separate terms and then simplifying the fractions in the individual terms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6x-4}{2} & = \\ \frac{6x}{2}-\frac{4}{2} & = \\ \frac{6}{2}\cdot x-\frac{4}{2} & = \\ 3x-2 & .\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Splitting a Rational Expression With Two Terms in the Numerator
canonical_examples.problem: Given that $\dfrac{6y − 1}{3} = ay + b,$  what are the values of $a$ and $b?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Splitting the fraction into separate terms and then simplifying the fractions in the individual terms, we get

$$
\eqalign{
		\dfrac{6y − 1}{3} &= \
		\dfrac{6y}{3} - \dfrac 1 3 &= \
		\dfrac{6}{3} \cdot y - \dfrac 1 3 &= \	
		2 \cdot y - \dfrac 1 3 &= \		
		2y - \dfrac 1 3 &.
	}
$$

Writing the above in the form $ay+b,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{{(2)}_{⏟}}_{a}y+{{(-\frac{1}{3})}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $a=2$ and $b=-\dfrac{1}{3}.$

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Splitting a Rational Expression With Three Terms in the Numerator
canonical_examples.problem: Given that $\dfrac{1 − 2a + 16b}{4} = p + qa + rb,$ what are the values of $p,$ $q,$ and $r?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Splitting the fraction into separate terms and then simplifying the fractions in the individual terms, we get

$$
\eqalign{
		\dfrac{1 − 2a + 16b}{4} &= \
		\dfrac 1 4 − \dfrac {2a} {4} + \dfrac {16b}{4} &= \
		\dfrac 1 4 − \dfrac {2} {4} \cdot a + \dfrac {16}{4} \cdot b &= \
		\dfrac 1 4 − \dfrac {1} {2} \cdot a + 4 \cdot b &= \		
		\dfrac 1 4 − \dfrac {a} {2} + 4b &= \
                \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}a + 4b &.
	}
$$

Writing the above in the form $p+qa+rb,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{{(\frac{1}{4})}_{⏟}}_{p}+{{(-\frac{1}{2})}_{⏟}}_{q}a+{{(4)}_{⏟}}_{r}b.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p=\dfrac{1}{4},$ $q=-\dfrac{1}{2},$ and $r=4.$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Fractions that contain multiple terms in the numerator and a single term in the denominator can be split into separate terms.

For example, 

$$
\eqalign{
		\dfrac {x + 2} {3} &= \
		\dfrac x 3 + \dfrac 2 3
	}
$$

and

$$
\eqalign{
		\dfrac {3a - 4b + 1} {5} &= \
		\dfrac {3a} 5 - \dfrac {4b} 5 + \dfrac 1 5.
	}
$$

Often, we're able to simplify the fractions in the individual terms, as follows:

$$
\eqalign{
		\dfrac {10x + 9} {2} &= \
		\dfrac {10x} {2} + \dfrac 9 2 &= \
		\dfrac {10} {2} \cdot x + \dfrac 9 2 &= \	
		5 \cdot x + \dfrac 9 2 &= \
		5x + \dfrac 9 2 
	}
$$
